svg.title: Patterns Are Tested in Practice
svg.desc: Sketch in perspective: in a workroom with a cutting table and a roll of paper behind them, one mannequin stands with its arms held out while a second holds a hatched paper sewing pattern against it. The pattern's sleeve stops short of the wrist, and the second figure is drawing a dashed line with a pencil to lengthen it. The paper sewing pattern is one of this site's patterns, the focus. It was cut on the table for someone else; holding it against a different person is the first half of the solution: apply the pattern in a piece besides the one that introduced it. The figure with its arms out is the practice the pattern meets, a real group or server. The short sleeve is a pattern that doesn't fit what happens in practice, and the pencil lengthening it is the second half: revise the pattern and say why. The metaphor: a pattern in the dressmaker's sense, a template that proves itself only when it's tried on, and is altered when it doesn't fit.
